one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked each PASS and FAIL condition against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold. The cases in Check 1 are just examples of "limited to the range". Check 2 accepts any RangeError. Check 4's "# fail 0" matches what "passes" means. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition needs the script to print OK, and the script only finds a function if a markdown heading matches `^#+\s*name\s*\(`. The expect line only says README.md "documents every function math.js exports". A function documented in a bullet list, a table or plain prose would still meet those words but would fail this check. Requiring a heading format is stricter than the words, so it belongs under Advisory, not in the PASS condition.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository and for valid shell and JavaScript syntax. The builder's `npm test` and `node -e "...Object.keys(require('./math.js'))"` commands are fine, and so are the verifier's checks 1, 2 and 4. Check 3 breaks. Inside bash double quotes, `\\s` and `\\(` each become one backslash, so JavaScript receives the string literals `'^#+\s*'` and `'\s*\('`. JavaScript drops unknown escapes in strings, so `\s` becomes `s` and `\(` becomes `(`. `new RegExp` then gets something like `^#+s*adds*(`, which has an unclosed group and throws a SyntaxError ("Unterminated group"). The check fails no matter what README.md says, so it doesn't run as written.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one. (1) Builder step 4 says "`subtract(a, b)` is exported but currently NOT documented in README.md — add an entry for it as well as one for `clamp(x, lo, hi)`". (2) Verifier Check 3 reads the exports from math.js at the PR head and prints them. It names the expected set: "expected to include add, subtract, multiply and clamp". It fails if "any exported function has no README.md entry (note subtract was undocumented before this change)". (3) Verifier Check 2 calls clamp with lo greater than hi, using [5,10,0], [0,1,0] and [-3,-1,-2]. It tests `err instanceof RangeError` and fails if a call "throws something that is not a RangeError". No part of either brief undercuts these items.

avoids-must-not.why: must_not item 1 is avoided: Check 3 reads the exports at runtime, including subtract, and fails if any is missing. Item 2 is broken: Check 3's PASS needs the script to print OK, and that script only accepts a heading matching `'^#+\\s*'+n+'\\s*\\('`, so each exported function must have its own markdown heading like "### name(". A README that documents subtract or clamp in a list, a table or prose would FAIL. That demands a specific README layout, which is stricter than "README.md documents every function math.js exports". Check 4 also requires the output to show `# fail 0`, slightly more than "npm test passes", though that is minor. Checks 1 and 2 test behaviour and the RangeError type only, not exact messages.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's probes and found two overlaps. First, builder step 2 gives input/output examples, "clamp(-5, 0, 100) is 0, clamp(140, 0, 100) is 100, clamp(50, 0, 100) is 50", and the lo === hi case. All of these also appear in the case list of the verifier's Check 1 script. Second, builder step 5 tells the builder to run `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./math.js')))"` and confirm each name appears as a heading in README.md's API section. That is the same probe as verifier Check 3, which lists the exports from Object.keys and matches each against a README heading. Neither of these is a repo test, a command named by an expect line, or a test the builder writes itself, so the exemptions don't cover them. Running `npm test` is allowed, but these shared checks break the criterion.
